location: Massage and spa near Ben Thanh Market, Ho Chi Minh City
text:
Step-by-Step Audio Guided Tour: Massage and spa near Ben Thanh Market, Ho Chi Minh City
Tour-Category: walking

Stop 1: Saigon Heritage Spa

Address:

Coordinates: 10.7763, 106.6959

Type/Specialty: Traditional Vietnamese Spa

Specific Examples: Herbal steam baths, traditional massages, and luxurious foot reflexology.

Orientation: We could confirm 2 stops along this route, so this tour has 2 stops rather than the 3 you asked for. This stroll will take you from the Saigon Heritage Spa to Saigon Spa, a distance of approximately 244 meters, traversing a bustling urban landscape where the modern city hums with life and history intertwines with the present. Your first stop is Saigon Heritage Spa. From Ben Thanh Market, head southeast on Le Loi Street, turn left onto Le Thanh Ton Street, and the spa will be on your right. You may notice the lively atmosphere of the local shops and cafes along the way. As you approach, the brick archway of Saigon Heritage Spa comes into view.

Saigon Heritage Spa has built its identity on a strict adherence to professionalism and legitimacy, setting itself apart from the everyday rhythms of the neighborhood. Just a few streets away, around Bến Thành and Bùi Viện, travelers often encounter touts offering suspiciously cheap massages, sometimes for as little as four to ten dollars a session. Visitors describe being escorted into private rooms by staff who then demand unexpectedly high tips, or discovering that cash has gone missing from their lockers. What begins as a search for relaxation can quickly turn into an ordeal of negotiation and subtle threat, leading to cautionary tales shared in online forums and by word of mouth.

In contrast, Saigon Heritage Spa has deliberately rejected these practices. It has cultivated a reputation as a mainstream, legitimate wellness business, where the focus remains on the client’s comfort rather than on extracting gratuities or exploiting uncertainty. The banyan tree in the courtyard is more than just a backdrop; it stands as a silent witness to the steady pulse of the community—the gentle shuffle of slippers on tile, quiet conversations between neighbors, and the subtle resistance to the transactional chaos that swirls just beyond the gates.

Directions: From Saigon Heritage Spa, head towards Le Loi Street and stroll past the bustling shops and cafes. Continue walking straight until you reach the corner with Phan Boi Chau Street, where you'll see Saigon Spa just a short distance ahead on your right. Enjoy the lively atmosphere as you make your way there! It is roughly 250 meters away.

Stop 2: Saigon Spa

Address:

Coordinates: 10.7750, 106.6941

Type/Specialty: Affordable Spa Services

Specific Examples: Relaxing body massages, facial treatments, and foot massages at budget-friendly prices.

Orientation: Stand just inside the hotel’s glass doors, where the carved balustrades and polished stone floors mark the threshold between the avenue’s bustle and the hush of Saigon Spa. From here, the contrast between the opulent Italian-inspired surfaces and the city’s more familiar textures is at its sharpest.

The Reverie Saigon, the hotel housing Saigon Spa, opened as a five-star property in the heart of District 1. Its presence within the Times Square building—a modern tower with frontage on both Dong Khoi and Nguyen Hue—signals a deliberate shift from the street’s customary rhythm. The marble beneath your shoes was chosen to echo the palazzi of Milan, not the tiled arcades of Ho Chi Minh City’s French era, and the chandeliers above are cut glass, catching the afternoon sun in colored prisms that scatter over lacquered wood and glossy stone.

This is not the neighborhood’s first brush with luxury. What sets Saigon Spa apart is its insistence on spectacle: panoramic views of the city skyline, borrowed from The Reverie’s upper floors, and a spatial choreography that invites guests to move between soaring lounge spaces and private treatment rooms, each lined with imported Italian furnishings.

In 2009, a very different kind of spectacle unfolded in Ho Chi Minh City when “HaMerotz LaMillion”—the Israeli reality competition known in English as “The Race to the Million”—chose Vietnam as one of seven countries for its inaugural season. Hosted by Raz Meirman, ten pairs of contestants swept through the city’s streets, their camera crews capturing both the luxury towers and the street-level markets that define District 1. Over ten legs and 42,000 kilometers, the show’s visit placed Saigon’s new generation of high-end venues, like this one, into a global television spotlight.

Within Saigon Spa’s walls, the city’s ambitions and contradictions are visible in every imported surface and every careful gesture of service. Where the race zigzagged from Kfar Truman to Otago, here the path is measured, the air cooled and quiet, and the spectacle is one of studied calm—a counterpoint to the city’s pulse below.

Across these stops, one thread runs through: the places that shape Massage and spa near Ben Thanh Market. Taken together, the stops add up to more than any one of them seen alone. Saigon Heritage Spa is one you might carry with you. That's 2 stops in all.
